[[OPEN_1]]Asia's Best Ayurvedic Retreat Since 1999[[CLOSE_1]][[OPEN_2]]Kairali-The Ayurvedic Healing Village, Palakkad, Kerala is one-of-its-kind of a holistic space, which offers traditional and authentic Ayurvedic therapies.[[CLOSE_2]]
A letter from K.V. Ramesh
Dear Guests,

Greetings from Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village, a haven where the ageless knowledge of Ayurveda is combined with the necessities of contemporary life. It gives me great pleasure to share with you the core values of Kairali, which are a dedication to holistic wellness, genuine Ayurvedic therapy, and the progress of humankind.

My vision for Kairali Ayurvedic Group has always been firmly based on the age-old science of Ayurveda, which I consider to be the best route to harmony and health. Growing up in a household immersed in Ayurvedic customs, I have personally seen the significant influence it has on people’s lives. This gave me the motivation to devote my life to protecting and introducing the world to this priceless legacy.

Authenticity and excellence have always been the cornerstones of Kairali. This idea is reflected in Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village. From the therapies and treatments to the calm, environmentally friendly setting, every element of this retreat has been planned to offer a fully immersive Ayurvedic experience. Here, we establish a sanctuary where visitors can discover tranquility, renewal, and balance by fusing traditional customs with contemporary hospitality standards.

Our goal goes beyond providing Ayurvedic care. It is to encourage a way of living that values mental, spiritual, and physical well-being. We aim to enable our guests to live better, more satisfying lives through our customized therapies, therapeutic diets, yoga classes, and meditation techniques.

Although Kairali Ayurvedic Group has become a well-known brand worldwide throughout the years, our principles have not changed. We are here to act as Ayurveda’s stewards, offering its therapeutic benefits to those who seek them while upholding the integrity that has established our reputation as a leading authority on holistic health.

To everyone who visits Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village, I extend my heartfelt gratitude. Your conviction in Ayurveda and Kairali motivates us to innovate and improve continuously. I welcome you to embark on this transforming journey of self-discovery, healing, and regeneration, guided by the timeless principles of Ayurveda.
Together, let us create a healthier, happier world.[[TAG_1]][[TAG_2]]Warm regards,[[TAG_3]][[OPEN_4]]K.V. Ramesh[[TAG_5]][[CLOSE_4]]Managing Director, Kairali Ayurvedic Group

Some health needs need a personalised programme rather than a listed one. This page only narrows things down — an Ayurvedic doctor assesses your health at consultation and tells you whether a suitable programme is available. Write to us in your own words; you do not need the right term or the right spelling.

Kerala, the magical tropical land where Ayurveda originated and whose natural beauty captivates everyone, is home to all Ayurvedic and Yoga devotees. Kairali - The Ayurvedic Healing Village in Palakkad, Kerala, is an escape refuge that provides patients with modern holistic therapy while adhering to the ancient principles of Yoga, Ayurveda, traditional Vedic traditions, and natural healing. With the presence of experienced Ayurveda and Yoga teachers, students can choose from a variety of training courses to meet their specific needs in this immersive Ayurvedic retreat in Kerala, India. THIRUVALATHOOR

It is a peaceful village in Kerala's Palakkad district that is rich in culture and spirituality. It is home to the historic Thiruvalathoor Mahadeva Temple, a famous shrine to Lord Shiva. The temple, known for its beautiful wooden carvings and traditional Kerala-style architecture, attracts both devout and architecture aficionados visiting nearby ayurvedic treatment packages in Kerala retreats. Thiruvalathoor, surrounded by thick greenery, has a serene ambiance that makes it an ideal location for spiritual searchers and nature enthusiasts.
Distance: 5.2 km
THENARI

Thenari is a lovely village in Kerala's Palakkad district that is well-known for its natural beauty and cultural significance. The town is famous for the Thenari Natural Spring, a sacred location with divine origins and ties to the Ramayana. Surrounded by rich greenery and quiet scenery, it is a peaceful getaway for those seeking spiritual serenity and a connection with nature while enjoying Kerala ayurvedic treatment stays. Its tranquil surroundings and historical significance make it a hidden gem among Kerala's rich cultural legacy.
Distance: 10 km
KATHAKALI

Kathakali is an ancient classical dance drama that depicts an act of devotion and the universal conflict between good and evil. With years of pedagogy, the dance form uses choreography, face, and hand movements to express Indian folklore and is often showcased to patients staying at the healing Village in Kerala, India.
MOHINIYATTAM

The classical dance form of Kerala, Mohiniyattam, finds its roots in Hindu Mythology. The undulating movements depict the dance of the enchantress Mohini. She made demons fall for her oscillating dance steps, passionate eyes, and graceful gestures to restore elixir. A delight for your eyes, women adorn simple, elegant gold-filigreed dresses in pure white or ivory while performing, often presented as a cultural highlight for patients on ayurvedic treatment packages in Kerala.

How can I find out whether this programme is right for me?

Not sure where to start? Speak with Priya or our sales team, share your details for physician review, or request a free consultation by video call, phone or email—whichever is convenient. After you submit your request, a coordinator will contact you to arrange the consultation.
Can I join while using inhalers or oxygen?
Tell the physician about your respiratory diagnosis, usual medicines and any oxygen or other equipment you use. Discuss whether a residential stay is appropriate and what support you would need.
Should I bring my CPAP or oxygen equipment?

It is preferable to bring your own CPAP or oxygen equipment. If you need the hospital to arrange it, please inform the team at least one week before admission. Arrangements require the doctor’s approval and are charged separately.
Can I continue my prescribed medicines?
Do not stop or change prescribed medicines on your own. Share a complete list of medicines and supplements with your treating clinicians and discuss any proposed Ayurvedic medicines with them.
What should I discuss with the physician before treatment?

Your consultation is an opportunity to understand the proposed treatment, its expected benefits, possible side effects and available alternatives. Share any concerns with your physician and keep the care team informed about how you feel during treatment.
What results can I realistically expect, and how long should I stay?

Treatment goals and the recommended duration of admission depend on your condition and the physician’s assessment. Your physician will discuss expected progress and review your response during treatment. Individual outcomes vary.
Can a companion stay with me?
Companion stays are considered case by case. Share your accommodation and assistance needs before admission so the team can confirm availability, arrangements and applicable charges.
What follow-up is included after discharge?

Your care includes four remote follow-up consultations with your treating physician within one year after discharge. Please schedule each appointment with your doctor; consultation dates are not fixed when you leave.
Do I need to submit medical reports before admission?
Pre-admission medical reports and physician clearance are required only for severe conditions, on a case-by-case basis. The team will confirm whether they are needed for your admission.
What support is available if I need help getting around or with daily activities?

Routine assistance, such as help walking or travelling by wheelchair between your room and the treatment centre, is available without requiring a dedicated attendant. If you need dedicated nursing or attendant support, this can be arranged at an additional cost based on the level of assistance required. Please share your needs before admission so the team can confirm suitable arrangements and charges.

Consultation:

A thorough consultation with the Ayurvedic doctor at the retreat. The doctor will assess your medical history, current symptoms, and overall health to understand the root cause of the bronchial condition.
Prakriti Assessment:

The Ayurvedic doctor will determine your unique body constitution (Prakriti) to personalize the treatment plan. This assessment helps in identifying the underlying imbalances causing the bronchial condition.
Diagnosis:
The doctor will diagnose the specific type of bronchial condition you have, such as asthma, bronchitis, or respiratory allergies. This helps in designing a targeted treatment approach.
Treatment Plan:

Based on the consultation and diagnosis, the Ayurvedic doctor will create a comprehensive treatment plan tailored to your individual needs. The plan may include herbal medications, dietary recommendations, lifestyle modifications, and specific Ayurvedic therapies.
Ayurvedic Therapies:

You may undergo various Ayurvedic therapies to support respiratory health. These therapies may include herbal steam inhalation, specialized massages, nasal irrigation, and breathing exercises to open up the respiratory passages and promote detoxification.
Herbal Medications:
The doctor will prescribe herbal formulations chosen for your symptoms; they are used alongside, not instead of, the inhalers or other medicines prescribed by your own doctor.
Follow-up & Lifestyle Recommendations:

Regular follow-up visits will be scheduled to monitor your progress and make any necessary adjustments to the treatment plan. The Ayurvedic doctor may provide guidance on lifestyle modifications, including dietary changes, exercise routines, stress management techniques, and sleep hygiene to support respiratory health.
Long-Term Maintenance:
Towards the end of your programme, the doctor will discuss long-term self-care, diet and routine to continue at home.
Holistic Approach:

Throughout the treatment process, the emphasis will be on addressing the underlying imbalances in the body and promoting overall well-being, as Ayurveda considers the mind-body connection in treating bronchial conditions.

Understanding Ayurveda
4 questions
What is Ayurveda, and how can it benefit me?

Ayurveda is a classical Indian system of medicine whose texts date back over two thousand years. It focuses on balance between body, mind and spirit through personalised therapies, nutrition, herbal treatments and lifestyle practices, and aims to address the underlying causes of imbalance rather than only symptoms.
How can I incorporate Ayurvedic principles into my daily life?
Wake up before sunrise and sleep by 10 PM
Practice mindful eating with fresh, seasonal foods
Stay hydrated with warm water throughout the day
Incorporate gentle movement like yoga or walking
Practice oil pulling and self-massage (abhyanga) with appropriate oils
Adjust your diet according to your dominant dosha (body constitution)
Our physicians provide personalised recommendations during your stay.
What are doshas, and why are they important?

Doshas are the three bodily energies—[[OPEN_1]]Vata[[CLOSE_1]] (air and space), [[OPEN_2]]Pitta [[CLOSE_2]](fire and water), and [[OPEN_3]]Kapha [[CLOSE_3]](earth and water)—that govern all physical and mental processes. Understanding your unique dosha composition helps determine the most effective treatments, diet, and lifestyle practices for your constitution. At Kairali, we conduct a thorough dosha assessment upon arrival to customize your wellness program.
Are Ayurvedic doctors real doctors?

Yes. Ayurvedic physicians in India complete a five-and-a-half-year BAMS (Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery) degree that includes clinical training in Ayurvedic and modern medical practice. Many pursue further specialisation (MD in Ayurveda) over an additional three years. Ayurvedic medicine is recognised by the WHO and regulated in India by the Ministry of AYUSH.
Read more on our [[OPEN_1]]Knowledge Centre[[CLOSE_1]].

Most programmes include two Ayurvedic therapies a day (one a day for the Preventive Health & Regenerative programme), alongside sunrise yoga and evening meditation. Kairali is not currently empanelled with Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY), CGHS or other government schemes, and we do not offer cashless tie-ups with private insurers. Many patients claim reimbursement afterwards by submitting our invoices and medical documents to their insurer.

We can provide detailed invoices, treatment summaries, prescriptions and admission/discharge notes to support a reimbursement claim, and can guide you on the documents insurers typically ask for. Final approval always depends on your insurer's policy.

More than 30 days before admission: full refund. 15 to 30 days before admission: 50% of the amount paid is refunded, less applicable transaction fees and taxes. Fewer than 15 days before admission, or a change of dates during the stay: no refund.

Before you travel
Should I fly to Coimbatore or Kochi?

Coimbatore (CJB) is the nearest airport, about one and a half to two hours by road, and the simplest arrival for most visitors. Choose Kochi / Cochin (COK) — about two and a half to three hours by road — when it offers a better international connection from your country.
How far is the nearest airport?

Coimbatore International Airport (CJB) is the nearest at around 62 km — about one and a half to two hours by car. Kochi / Cochin International Airport (COK) is around 115 km away, about two and a half to three hours by road.
Do you arrange pick-up from the airport or railway station?

Yes. The hospital can arrange a private car for arriving patients. Message our patient care team on WhatsApp, or call the main line, and share your arrival date, time and flight or train number. A team member will confirm the driver and vehicle details.
How will I recognise the driver?
A Kairali representative waits for you in the arrivals area with a name-board. You receive the driver’s name and vehicle details before you land, so you know exactly who is picking you up.
Is pick-up available for late-evening arrivals?
Yes. A pre-arranged transfer is recommended for late arrivals, when local roads are quiet. Share your flight details in advance and your driver will wait for you at any hour.
Can I come by train?

Yes. Palakkad Junction (PGT) is the recommended station, around 18 km away — about a 35-minute drive. Taxis are available at the station, or send us your train number and arrival time and we will pick you up.
Is the trip safe for a solo traveller?

Kerala is among the calmest regions of India, and English is widely spoken. With a pre-arranged transfer you are met by a named driver, so there is no need to look for a taxi on arrival. Many of our patients travel to us alone.
Can you accommodate a wheelchair or a caregiver?
Yes. A wheelchair-accessible vehicle and an accompanying caregiver can be arranged. Please tell us your requirements at booking so the right vehicle is ready.
Do I need an Indian visa?

Most international visitors need a valid passport and an Indian visa or an eligible e-Visa. Requirements vary by nationality and can change — please check the official Government of India visa portal before you travel.
Is this a hospital or a spa?

Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village is an NABH-accredited Ayurvedic hospital. Care is led by registered Ayurvedic physicians, and every treatment programme begins with a clinical consultation. It is not a spa.

What diseases can be treated with Panchakarma procedures?

Panchakarma is used in Ayurveda as part of the care of many conditions, e.g. Joint disorders (Rheumatoid arthritis), Musculoskeletal (Low backache), Dermatological (Psoriasis), Neurological (Paralysis, Migraine), Respiratory disorders (Bronchial asthma), Gynecological disorders (Leucorrhea), Psychiatric, Geriatric, etc. It may also be used to support quality of life in long-term conditions. Your physician will advise whether it is suitable for you.
Who should seek Panchakarma?

Any person in the age group of 18 to 70 can seek or be prescribed for the process of panchakarma. Panchakarma is also helpful for smoking and other de-addiction initiatives as it clears unwanted toxins to curb the desire for intoxicants. Vata, pitta and kapha imbalances in the body also require panchakarma.
Does Panchakarma offer instant relief for health conditions?
Generally not! Panchakarma relieves the body of its toxins, and the effects begin to show up gradually; although one finds the lightness and relief in muscular stiffness.
What will be my diet during Panchakarma treatment and after?
Light vegetarian diets are prescribed during the panchakarma treatment. After the process, depending upon the pravrrati (inclinations), a specific diet is prescribed.
Are Panchakarma procedures only for individuals with diseases?
No. Panchakarma therapies are helpful for healthy persons also for promoting good health and preventing diseases. It is helpful in expelling doshas accumulated due to seasonal variations.

About [[OPEN_1]]Paralysis Recovery & Rehabilitation Therapy[[CLOSE_1]]

Paralysis is the loss of muscle function in part or all of the body and is often accompanied by a loss of sensation. It occurs due to disruptions in the communication between the brain and muscles, typically caused by conditions affecting the nervous system. Common causes include stroke, spinal cord injuries, traumatic brain injuries, multiple sclerosis, and infections like polio.

Paralysis can be classified as partial (affecting some muscles) or complete, and it can be temporary or permanent depending on the underlying cause. It is further categorized by the affected area, such as paraplegia (lower body) or quadriplegia (all four limbs).
Early diagnosis, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, and advanced treatments can significantly improve quality of life.

History of [[OPEN_1]]Postpartum Rejuvenation Therapy Program[[CLOSE_1]]

In ancient Indian households, this phase, known as the “Sutika Kala,” was treated with immense care, recognizing the physical and emotional transformation a woman undergoes after childbirth. Families followed a meticulously crafted regimen involving nourishing meals, therapeutic massages, and calming rituals to ensure recovery and long-term well-being.

Ayurvedic texts emphasized restoring balance to the body, strengthening the uterus, and replenishing energy reserves. Practices like oil baths and gentle detox therapies were handed down through generations, offering holistic healing.
At Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village, we carry forward this timeless tradition, offering personalized care that blends ancient wisdom with modern needs.

About [[OPEN_1]]Treatment for Ayurveda Skin Vitality Revival[[CLOSE_1]]

The Ayurvedic Skin Vitality Revival Treatment at Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village is a therapeutic skin-care program rooted in classical Ayurvedic principles. Designed to support the health and natural glow of the skin, this treatment is ideal for those experiencing dryness, dullness, premature aging, pigmentation, or chronic skin conditions.

It combines detoxifying Panchakarma therapies, specialized herbal applications, and nourishing massages using traditional Ayurvedic oils. The treatment not only addresses external concerns but also focuses on balancing internal imbalances—often the root cause of skin issues—through dietary guidance, lifestyle modification, and stress management techniques. The therapy also includes attention to circulation and digestion as part of skin care.
Approach [[OPEN_1]]for Treating Ayurveda Skin Vitality Revival[[CLOSE_1]]

Experience the holistic Ayurvedic approach to herbal skin detox in Ayurveda at Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village. With over [[VAR_1]] years of experience, we focus on addressing the root cause rather than just the symptoms. Ayurveda identifies skin ailments as dosha imbalances (Vata, Pitta, Kapha) and strives to restore balance through personalized treatments. Our skilled Ayurvedic doctors assess each patient’s constitution and create tailored treatment plans incorporating therapies and herbal medicines. Our therapies include Panchakarma detox, rejuvenating herbal oil massages, and specialized skin treatments for cleansing, nourishing, and revitalizing the skin. We also recommend dietary and lifestyle changes to support overall well-being. We prioritize natural, plant-based ingredients and prepare herbal medicines following Ayurvedic principles for purity and effectiveness. Choose Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village for an authentic Ayurvedic approach to skin concerns that looks at underlying causes and your overall well-being.

[[OPEN_1]]Why[[CLOSE_1]] Treatment for Ayurveda Skin Vitality Revival?

[[OPEN_1]]◆[[CLOSE_1]]Holistic Ayurvedic Approach- By balancing the doshas (Pitta, Kapha, and Vata) and removing toxins (Ama) from the body, Kairali aims to treat the underlying causes of skin conditions.
[[OPEN_1]]◆[[CLOSE_1]]Natural & Herbal Remedies- Treatments include high-quality herbal formulations, oils, and pastes made using traditional Ayurvedic processes.

[[OPEN_1]]◆[[CLOSE_1]]Panchakarma Therapy for Skin Detox- Panchakarma treatments like Raktamokshana (blood purification) and Virechana (purgation) are traditionally used for cleansing in Ayurvedic skin care.

Teachers
Take a transformational journey to Kerala, India as you embrace the ancient healing science of Ayurveda.
Touted ‘God’s own Country’ Kerala is India’s luscious jewel abundant with herb and tea plantations, scenic beaches and breathtaking backwaters.

Our retreat takes place at the award winning [[OPEN_1]][[OPEN_2]]Kairali Ayurvedic Healing Village[[CLOSE_2]][[CLOSE_1]] well away from the hustle and bustle of India’s City’s. People come here from all corners of the globe to experience profound healing and it’s also where the Indian people themselves come to restore balance, health and inner harmony.

Your retreat begins with a detailed consultation with an Ayurvedic doctor who will carefully design [[OPEN_1]]Ayurveda[[CLOSE_1]] experiences to treat, heal, restore and rejuvenate your health. Ayurveda is an elaborate healing system of India, a science of life based on the laws of nature. Its derived from the Sanskrit words Ayur(life) and Veda(knowledge), it traces its origins to about 50 centuries.
2019 record photograph

Each day on retreat begins with a yoga session and includes 2 x Daily Ayurveda Treatment (prescribed especially for you by the Doctor), meditation, nourishing food and relaxation. Dotted throughout your retreat you will experience an Ayurvedic cooking class, mindfulness workshops and Yoga Nidra which will arm you with invaluable life skills to return home with.

Upon our arrival in India, before we embark on our Ayurvedic Healing Journey we spend 2 nights in Fort Kochi just 45mins from the international airport. There will be a full day to explore this eclectic neighbourhood at your leisure including the lively spice and antique market and local art scene. After meandering the well preserved colonial streets on foot or by rickshaw we finish our day taking in an unforgettable sunset as the fisherman return with the days catch. For dinner we’ll be feasting on Kerala’s signature curries with new and old friends.

Have you ever wondered why people gain weight at different rates, walk at different speeds and are prone to different health problems? According to the ancient Indian healing system Ayurveda, the answer lies in your constitution type or Dosha. This quiz will help you identify your Dosha, discover which elements govern you and learn how to live the optimum lifestyle for your constitution type.

Kairali Ayurvedic Village – Personalised Wellness Formula

Kairali Ayurvedic Group’s flagship ayurvedic destination, Kairali-The Ayurvedic Healing Village, Palakkad, Kerala is one-of-its-kind of a holistic space, which offers traditional and authentic Ayurvedic therapies, treatments and medications along with Yoga and Meditation. The healing village sits at the foot of Nilgiri and Annamalai ranges (Western Ghats). Set amidst mountains, forests, fertile valley and rivers are the 30 premium villas, which are forever surrounded by the fragrance of Pala trees. In compliance with Vaastu Shastra, the villas add on to the restorative and curative ambience. The Ayurvedic Healing Village also boasts of Red Oxide flooring, a rare Valambari Conch shell and a gentle stream flowing around every villa. Yoga, Meditation, Astrology, Palmistry, nutrition, therapy, spiritual training and traditional Indian rituals (pujas) are part of the routine at the retreat. The Ayurvedic Healing Village is the epitome of Kairali’s skill in concept hospitality – a perfectly intuitive design born of timeless wisdom. Time spent at this inspiring jungle sanctuary will leave you wondering whether you are experiencing the height of modern holistic luxury, or have travelled far into India’s distant past.

Ananda Lahari Retreat Ananda – Happiness Lahari – Wave

In our everyday lives, we encounter and handle numerous situations, whether they involve family, work, relationships, or other obligations. This retreat aims to prepare you to handle life and its circumstances with joy and ease.

By utilizing Ayurveda and the teachings and insights of Yoga, you will achieve harmony and equilibrium between your body and mind, as well as with those around you and your surroundings. These time-honored traditions present ways to improve our contemporary way of living and give you a structure to examine existence and experience life to its maximum potential.
The Ananda Lahari Retreat provides a chance to embark on a genuine and thrilling spiritual adventure in India, fostering a realm abundant with love, light, and joy.
What is the Ananda Lahari Retreat?

The Ananda Lahari Retreat offers a journey to well-being via healing, self-exploration, and transformation of both mind and body. It is ideal for yoga practitioners and instructors at any level seeking to enhance their practice and uncover profound health, wellness, and a connection to their authentic self.

Our authentic complete immersion program lasts 7 days at the stunning Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village in Kerala. Throughout a week, you will immerse yourself in the complete experience of yogic living: engaging in sunrise meditations and asana practice, participating in discussions on Vedanta and philosophy, practicing yoga nidra, exploring Sanskrit and tantra rituals, along with following an Ayurvedic diet and enjoying daily massages and treatments, you will thoroughly incorporate the yogic lifestyle into your life.

This personal journey will allow you to delve into historical wisdom and traditions and subsequently weave their usage into your everyday life. It is probably one of the most impactful experiences for the future health and wellness of your mind, body, and spirit. You will enhance your health and well-being while also enriching your self-awareness and understanding of the universe, building lifelong connections and friendships, and creating numerous lasting memories.
Where will this Journey Take Me?
A collage of cottages, a garden bench and a flower arrangement.

Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village was selected among the top 50 wellness destinations of the world by National Geographic Traveller. The village is situated in Palakkad, just a few kilometres from the world’s biggest mountain pass between Kerala and Tamil Nadu. This award-winning spa and retreat facility is nestled in a luscious landscape of 600 coconut palms.
Time spent at this unique paradise will allow you to experience the authentic healing practices of ancient India while relaxing in the lap of modern holistic luxury.
What Will I Experience?
Therapists giving a massage.
The term ‘Ayur’ translates to life, while ‘Veda’ refers to knowledge, thus, Ayurveda signifies ‘knowledge of the science of living’.

You will undergo a comprehensive program of genuine Ayurvedic treatments designed to achieve harmony among body, mind, and spirit. A group of Ayurvedic physicians will assess your health and determine the optimal rejuvenation plan for the week. It might be Abhyangam massages (where two therapists rhythmically and simultaneously apply herbal oils) or other targeted therapies like dhaara to achieve optimal wellness and restore equilibrium in you.
Our sessions on Ayurveda and the visit to Kairali’s Ayurvedic Product Factory will give you a basis for understanding the use of Ayurveda in contemporary life.
People practising yoga on mats.
The term Yoga comes from the Sanskrit word yuj, signifying “to join” or “to unite.” It is the harmony of the body, mind, and spirit, as well as the link between the personal self and awareness.

Kairali is an ideal destination for those looking to explore the depths of yoga, its historical context, foundational principles, and relevance in contemporary life. The retreat will include workshops for all levels, encompassing yoga philosophy, vedanta, sanskrit, tantra, and meditation. By consciously incorporating these principles into our lives, we can adopt a unified strategy to create a lifestyle that fosters genuine health and longevity.
The philosophy and wisdom of yoga, which is over 5,000 years old, is extensive. In our workshops, we will assist you in understanding ancient philosophies and incorporating them into your daily life.
Broaden your understanding of Vedanta, yogic philosophy, kundalini, meditation, Sanskrit, and tantra.

Every workshop will involve a free discussion and examination of ideas, along with actionable advice for applying them in your daily life, allowing you to incorporate yoga more completely into your routine.

Experience Kerala’s Rich Culture – Dance, Music and Martial Arts
Explore Kerala’s cultural heritage with Kathakali, Bharatanatyam, Mohiniyattam, Chenda, and Kalari at Kairali Healing Village, Witness traditions come alive.
5 minutes
Things to Do in Kerala

The ancient and classical dance drama Kathakali depicts a devotional act and the universal conflict between good and evil. The dance style uses choreography, hand gestures, facial expressions, and years of training to portray Indian tradition.

Makeup and headdresses, followed by colorful costumes worn by different characters, are the symbolism of Kathakali, which demands a great deal of work. Folk mythologies, religious traditions, and the spiritual concepts of Hindu epics are all exemplified by Kathakali, an otherworldly and wonderful aspect that makes the entire dance extraordinary.

Dance is unique because of its storytelling style, superb footwork, and striking facial and hand movements that are complemented by vocal and musical performances. The ancient martial arts and athletic customs that are common in Kerala and the surrounding areas are reflected in the elaborate and vibrant makeup, distinctive face masks, and costumes, as well as the unrivaled style and moves. Traditionally, male dancers perform it.

Mohiniyattam, Kerala’s traditional dance style, has its origins in Hindu mythology. The enchantress “Mohini” is shown dancing in the flowing motions. With her elixir-restoring beautiful motions, ardent eyes, and oscillating dancing steps, she captivated devils. It’s a visual treat, with women wearing modest, exquisite dresses with gold filigree in ivory or pure white. This impression goes really well with the melodious music that goes with the dance. Facial expressions are highly valued in this dance style, similar to Kathakali, and dancers must be excellent actors to convey them in the best possible way. Popular throughout the Chera dynasty from the ninth to the twelfth centuries, Mohiniyattam is a highly stylized, feminine dancing style.
Bharatanatyam

South India is the birthplace of Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest styles of classical dance. “Bharatanatyam” is the name of a dance style that incorporates bhava(expression), tala(rhythm), and raga (melody). Hindu religious themes and spiritual concepts are illustrated through dancers’ amazing footwork and striking gestures. Among its repertoire of performances are Nrita (Pure dance), Nritya(expressive dance), and Natya(dramatic storytelling). Across the nation, the dance style serves as an inspiration for a variety of artistic mediums, such as sculpture and painting. It is a challenging dance style that calls for dedication, years of practice, intense facial expressions, exceptional acting ability, and intricate foot and body movements.
Chenda

Among Kerala’s many percussion art forms, the Chenda, a percussion instrument, holds a distinct place. The magnificent instrument is seen as inevitable and is utilized extensively in practically every Keralan event. The player beats intricate rhythms on the drum surface using specialized sticks. The instrument’s cylindrical wooden body is composed of cassia fistula, sugar palm, white teak, and jackfruit tree wood. The unique feature is that the wood is from the centre of the jackfruit tree.
Kalari

Kalari Payattu is a martial art practiced in a unique type of gymnasium called Kalari. The unique training in “Marma”, or the art of understanding and triggering each of the 107 energy spots in the human body, is a significant aspect of Kalari. The purpose of these marmas, or vital places, is to restore the body’s resources and balance its energy flows. Thus, Kalari transforms the practitioner into a self-healer as well as a warrior who may use his healing abilities to assist others.

Kalari has its own Ayurvedic medical specialty that treats injuries, physical ailments, and dislocations. These methods are used in conjunction with massages to relieve muscle soreness and improve body flexibility. Although Kalari’s popularity declined in the 17th century, it is currently fast increasing in the state of Kerala.

How does Kairali compare to modern wellness fusion retreats?

Resorts like Atmantan integrate mixed healing systems, whereas Kairali practices pure classical Ayurveda under medical supervision. With certified therapists and round-the-clock doctor support, treatments remain rooted in Ayurvedic science, producing measurable relief in short, structured therapy cycles.
What advantages does Kairali have over luxury wellness retreat?

While Ananda focuses on luxury spa wellness in the mountains, Kairali emphasizes clinical Ayurvedic healing at its source—Kerala. Treatments are supported by on-site herbal preparation and physician-guided therapy plans, offering deeper therapeutic outcomes rather than spa-centric experiences.
How is Kairali different from Ayurvedic treatment centers?

Unlike chains such as Kerala Ayurveda, which offer clinic-based therapies, Kairali offers a complete residential healing village experience. Guests stay, eat, heal, and recover within one integrated setting, guided personally by doctors and trained Ayurvedic practitioners through structured recovery programs.
Why choose Kairali over strict traditional Ayurvedic properties?

Retreats like Kalari Kovilakom follow highly rigid classical routines. Why the Monsoon Matters in Ayurveda

Also known as Karkidaka Ayurveda Treatment, this is a traditional monsoon Ayurvedic treatment from Kerala. Classical Ayurveda regards the cool, humid monsoon as a traditional season for detoxification and rejuvenation therapies directed at the tissues and doshas (Vata, Pitta, Kapha).

Attractions 15 Kilometres | Kerala | Palakkad | Tourist Attractions
Visit top attractions near Kairali, including Malampuzha Dam, Rock Garden, Fantasy Park, and Chittur Gurumadam for a mix of nature, history, and adventure.
Attractions (15 Kms & Below)

Padmashree Nekchand Saini, a world-renowned sculptor who also designed India’s first rock garden in Chandigarh, created the Malampuzha Rock Garden. It is a true work of art because the artifacts on display are constructed entirely of waste materials such as granites, stones, broken bangles, melamine dishware, broken tiles, power insulators, and so on. It supports a calm planted garden where you can relax and be captivated by the panoramic magnificence of the park’s surrounding mountain ranges.

Chittur Gurumadam, located on the banks of the Sokanasdini River in Thekkegramam near Arikkode, is a memorial to Thunchath Ramanujan Ezhuthachan, the father of the Malayalam language. Ezhuthachan replicated the two major Sanskrit epics, the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, in Malayalam. A Shri chakra, a stylus, wooden slippers, a few antique manuscripts, and some of the idols he adored are displayed here.
Fantasy Park Malampuzha Dam in Palakkad

Fantasy Park, located near Malampuzha Dam in Palakkad, is Kerala’s first amusement park, and it is a fun place for the entire family. There are numerous entertainment alternatives available, including 16D Cine Magic rides, Boomerang Water Ride, Multi Slide, Planetarium, Wave Pool, Para Trooper, Dragon Coaster, Rain Disco, Fanta Tub, Super Splash, Tora Tora, Virtual Waterfall, Pirate Ship, Merry-go-round, and more.

The Malampuzha Reservoir is a popular tourist attraction. It is bordered by lovely gardens, amusement parks, fish-shaped aquariums, and a snake park. Boating, pedal boats, rowing boats, water scooters, motor boats, and fishing are all available for a low cost.

Although Palakkad is a small town, its development into a significant tourist destination is unsurprising given its rich culture, abundant greenery, and diverse flora and wildlife. There are magnificent and amazing spots near Palakkad that you will not regret visiting because the trip will be worthwhile. Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village provides trips that allow you to discover the magnificent beauty of Kerala.
Tiled temple gateway with a Malayalam signboard beside a rural road among coconut palms

This ancient 14th-century temple, also known as Moonnumoorthy temple, was built on the banks of Thootha, a tributary of the Bharathapuzha river. The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and Narayana. An elegant Koothambalam, or temple theatre, is claimed to have been erected on the structure around the 15th century.
Forest waterfall cascading over dark rocks into a clear green pool

The Meenvallam waterfalls, which originate at the mouth of the Thuppanadu River, are a hidden treasure in Kerala. This unique combination of mesmerizing beauty and panoramic splendor is a ten-step waterfall where the water drops from about 20 to 25 feet. The upper eight steps of the waterfall are hidden inside a lush forest, while the lower two are open to visitors.
Long concrete dam wall running beside a wide reservoir under a clear blue sky

Meenkara is a tourist destination because of the dam built across the Meenkara River, a sub-tributary of Gayathripuzha that eventually merges into the Bharathapuzha River. The grandeur and pure beauty of this dam are a visual feast for spectators. It is an excellent picnic place, with a fish farm and lovely gardens.
A dam releasing water into the reservoir below, with wooded hills behind

Surrounded by the enthralling beauty of mountains, dense evergreen forests, and cotton clouds, Kanjirapuzha Dam is an alluring natural dam. The reservoir has a total of three islands within it and is composed of plenty of fish which is a sight to behold. If you are looking for peace amidst the divine mysticism of nature, you must visit this place once in Kerala.
Road along a reservoir dam embankment leading towards mist-covered green hills

Constructed across the Meenichiladipuzha and Padipuzha rivers, Pothundy Dam is considered to be one of the oldest dams in India. The core wall of this dam is made with a mixture of jaggery and quick lime which makes it unique among others. Pothundy Dam is an ideal destination for those looking for picnics or a one-day trip. You can also visit nearby attractions such as Padagiri, Kilakettara, Nemmara, and Kollengode.

Palakkad, with its diverse natural scenery and man-made wonders, has carved its place into the Kerala tourism landscape. It has become one of the most popular destinations for adventure, trekking, and getting close to nature. People from all over the world are drawn to this place. Apart from the sights found inside and near Palakkad’s borders, there are additional fantastic tourist places to visit if you are willing to venture a bit further into the wilderness.
Reservoir ringed by forested hills and a rocky peak, seen from a green hillside

Nelliyampathy, the ‘Queen of Palakkad Hills’, is a lovely place surrounded by wispy clouds and has a charm all its own. The beauty of this location, which is made up of orange plantations and evergreen forests, will captivate you, making it ideal for a relaxing vacation. The area is famed for its tea and coffee plantations, cardamom plantations, waterfalls, and beautiful weather. It is a small but beautiful hill station that is ideal for trekking, Jeep safaris, and bird and animal watching.
Traditional Kerala temple with tiered tiled roofs and carved wooden walls on a sandy courtyard

Kalamandalam, a world-renowned Kathakali training facility, is based near Cheruthuruthy hamlet. Aside from being a renowned Kathakali centre, it also offers training in other performing arts like Mohiniyattam, Koodiyattam, Thullal, and Nangiarkoothu. Training in voice and percussive instruments is also available here. Kalamandalam, founded in 1930 by Malayalam poet Vallathol Narayana Menon, reflects the simplicity, purity, and ethnic environment in which these arts have flourished over generations.
Kerala temple complex with a tiled pyramidal shrine and low surrounding buildings

Thrithala, known for its medieval ruins, is of significant archeological significance. Notable cultural monuments are the ruins of a massive mud fort with a deep laterite moat and the Siva temple. The Kattil Madom Temple, a domed edifice composed of granite slabs on the Pattambi-Guruvayoor route, is a Buddhist monument thought to date from the ninth or tenth centuries. The temple most likely represents the transition from Chola to Pandya architecture.
Shallow rocky river running through dense greenery below a forested hill

Attappadi is a large mountain valley located near the headwaters of the Bhavani River, below the Western Ghats’ Nilgiri Hills. Its limits extend from Coimbatore district in Tamil Nadu in the east to Karimba, Pottassery, and Mannarghat in the west, and from the Nilgiris in the north to Palghat taluk in the south. These hills are rich in flora and wildlife, and they greet visitors with a sense of freshness and give you complete serenity and joy.
Curving stone ramparts of a hill fort above green valleys and a distant lake

Silent Valley National Park is Kerala’s second-largest national park, covering a core area of 236.74 square kilometers. The park is one of the last untouched areas of the South-Western Ghats Mountains. The place is completely silent, even without the chirping of cicadas. Road transportation is only available up to Mukkali, which is 24 kilometers from the park, and the remainder of the journey must be completed by foot.
Large ochre-walled temple with gold-finialled tiled roofs and people crossing the open ground

Guruvayur is regarded as one of Kerala’s most important pilgrimage sites. Sree Krishna Temple is well-known for its curative qualities and attracts an incredible number of pilgrims each year. It is known as the Dwaraka of the South and is notable for its ‘Thulabharam’ offering, in which devotees are weighed against bananas, sugar, jaggery, and coconuts in proportion to their weight. The annual Guruvayur Festival, held in February-March, begins with an elephant race. The festival is unavoidable. Not to mention the Guruvayur Devaswom Elephant Sanctuary, located barely 3 kilometers from the temple and one of the world’s largest elephant sanatoriums, also known as Punnathurkotta.
Wooden treehouse on stilts with a blue slide in a leafy garden

Parambikulam Wildlife Sanctuary is a 391-square-kilometre protected area in Chittur Taluk. It is spread throughout Anaimalai Hills and Nelliampathy Hills. The Kerala Parambikulam National Park is covered in bamboo, rosewood, and sandalwood trees, and it is home to a diverse range of animals such as leopards, wild dogs, sloths, crocodiles, civets, tigers, elephants, wild boar, barking deer, spotted deer, monkeys, langurs, porcupines, and macaques.

Tiled-roof heritage palace with whitewashed walls beside a still water-filled moat

Thiruvalathoor is known for its ancient temple, which features excellent woodwork and stone sculptures. According to legend, an army of Gods built the temple’s outside wall, but because they were unable to finish it by daylight, they left it unfinished so that humanity would not notice it. Despite continuous human efforts to erect the wall, it remains unfinished.
Tall coconut palms lining the edge of a green paddy field

Thenari is a holy shrine located on the Pollachi Road from Palakkad town. The famed Sree Rama temple in Thenari is devoted to Lord Rama, and the natural spring in front of the old temple is revered as sacred as the waters of the holy Ganges. It is claimed that Lord Rama and Sita visited this location during their exile.
Hillside complex of multi-storey buildings around a Hindu temple spire and lawned garden

Jainimedu is a Jain temple located 3 kilometres from Palakkad’s centre. It was built in the 15th century. This temple was built by Jain Leader Inchana Satur and is dedicated to Chandraprabha, a Tirthankar of the Jain religion. This granite marvel of history is 32 feet long and 20 feet wide, with images of the Jain Thirthankaras and Yakshinis. Kumaranasan, a highly regarded Malayalam poet, penned his famous poem Veenapoovu (The Fallen Flower) at a Jain residence near this temple.
Laterite fort ramparts and bastion surrounded by a water-filled moat and lawns

Tipu’s Fort, also known as the Palakkad Fort, stands high in the middle of Palakkad. Hyder Ali, the monarch of the Mysore region, built this fort in 1766, and it is now a protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India. The fort has an open-air auditorium called “Rappadi” on its vast grounds. Inside, there is a little temple called Anjaneya Swamy Temple, and on the opposite side is a children’s park. It is one of the best-preserved forts in southern India.
Carved stone pillars with lion sculptures lining the paved corridor of an ancient temple
Kalpathy is one of Kerala’s oldest ‘Brahmin Agraharams’, situated in the heart of the town. The ‘Ratholsavam’ event, which takes place in the middle of November, is well-known in Palakkad.

Twenty days in four movements: foundations and Abhyangam; the classical therapies one by one; Panchakarma, medicines and dietetics; consultation practice, professional etiquette and examinations.

Days 1–5 — Foundations and Abhyangam: introduction, history and branches; Panchamahabhuta, Tridosha, Saptadhatu, Agni and Ama; health and disease; Abhyangam learnt from head and neck to the full body; Shirodhara and Nasyam in theory and practice.

Days 6–10 — Therapies in depth: Dhatu, Mala, Agni and Ama and the classification of disease; Dinacharya and Ritucharya; human anatomy and physiology; Podikizhi, Udwarthanam, Udhgarshanam and Kativasti; Roga and Rogi Pareeksha; Prakriti definition, analysis questionnaire and body-constitution analysis.

Days 11–15 — Dietetics, medicines and Panchakarma: Ahara and Vihara, Dravyaguna and the actions of substances (Guna, Virya, Vipaka, Prabhava); classical and proprietary medicines with a products demonstration; Snehanam and Swedanam, Poorva and Pashchat Karma, Vamanam, Virechanam, Nasyam, Vasti and Raktamoksha with their precautions and contraindications; Njavara Kizhi and Elakizhi prepared and applied.

Days 16–19 — Consultation and practice: Nadee Pareeksha and vital readings; Ayurvedic wellness consultation, body-constitution analysis and programme development with case-file preparation; complete revision of theory and practical; therapy etiquette, treatment-room and tray preparation, steam-generator and pharmacy operations, statutory requirements and the regulatory bodies of Ayurveda.
Day 20 — Examinations: an objective theory paper and a practical examination, then the concluding session and certification.
Format: eighty hours over twenty days — theory and practical every day — with examinations at the end.
Who it suits: people from the healthcare and wellness sector, lifestyle consultants and therapists who want a recognised practitioner certificate.

After the course: successful candidates may take part in projects and hands-on work at Kairali's domestic and international centres; outstanding candidates may be considered for Ayurvedic Wellness Consultant roles.
Stay: twenty nights in the hospital's villas, charged per night under the training tariff — Deluxe Villa ₹18,410 single / ₹30,530 double ($263 / $436; €230 / €382).
Eight therapies: perform Abhyangam, Shirodhara, Nasyam, Podikizhi, Udwarthanam, Kativasti, Njavara Kizhi and Elakizhi to the hospital's standard.
Consultation: examine a patient (Roga and Rogi Pareeksha, Nadee Pareeksha), analyse body constitution and develop a programme with a case file.
Panchakarma: explain the two aspects of Panchakarma, its five procedures and their precautions.
Dietetics and medicines: apply Dravyaguna and Ahara–Vihara principles and know the classical and proprietary preparations.
Professional practice: run a treatment room to the hospital's etiquette and understand the statutory framework of Ayurveda.
Healthcare professionals, wellness consultants and therapists, and serious Ayurveda students seeking practitioner-level training.
Do I need prior Ayurveda training?
The programme is designed for people already in healthcare or wellness. It starts from first principles, so formal prior Ayurveda study is not required.
Is there an examination?
Yes. Day 20 is an objective theory paper and a practical examination; the practitioner certificate follows successful completion.
Does the course lead to work with Kairali?
Outstanding candidates may be considered for Ayurvedic Wellness Consultant roles at Kairali's centres. This is a consideration, not a guarantee.
Is this a medical degree?
No. It is a practitioner certificate for lifestyle consultancy and therapy, not a medical degree or a licence to practise medicine.

Ten days, each pairing a theory block with a practical block. Therapies are learnt in stages — head, neck and body, then the prone position, then full body — before the next therapy is introduced.

Day 2 — Panchamahabhuta, Tridosha, Saptadhatu, Agni and Ama; Abhyangam in the prone position.
Day 3 — Swastha Lakshana, the Trigunas, health and disease; full-body Abhyangam.
Day 4 — Treatment modalities and Shirodhara theory; Shirodhara practical.
Day 5 — Abhyangam and Shirodhara review, Nasyam theory; Nasyam practical.
Day 6 — Dosha, Dhatu and Mala, the classification of disease, Podikizhi theory; Podikizhi preparation, tying and application.
Day 7 — Dinacharya, Ritucharya, anatomy and physiology; Podikizhi practical.
Day 8 — Ahara and Vihara, the basics of Dravyaguna, anatomy part two; Udwarthanam theory and practical.
Day 9 — Roga and Rogi Pareeksha, an introduction to Panchakarma, Kativasti theory; Kativasti practical.
Day 10 — Prakriti basics and the analysis questionnaire; review of all therapies and closing Q&A.
Format: forty hours — two hours of theory and two hours of practical daily over ten days — with group yoga and meditation sessions.
Who it suits: therapists, wellness counsellors and the wider wellness fraternity; yoga instructors and holistic practitioners.

Is the online consultation really complimentary?

Who will I actually be speaking with?

Why do you ask for a health summary after I request?

Is my health information kept private?
Yes. What you share is used only to arrange and conduct your consultation and is read by our medical team. We never sell your information, and we handle it in line with our
. Please note that if you contact us by WhatsApp or email, your messages pass through those services.
Do I have to travel to Kerala?
No. The consultation is online — by WhatsApp video or call — at a time we agree. If a residential treatment programme is appropriate for you, the physician will explain the options.
Will I be pressured to book a treatment programme?

No. The physician’s role is to give you an honest, considered view — and sometimes that view is that our programmes are not appropriate for your situation, in which case we will tell you so plainly. There is no sales follow-up attached to the consultation; what happens next is entirely your decision.
Can I arrange the consultation for my parent or spouse?

Yes, and many patients’ families do. Select “A family member” in the request form, and you are welcome to join the call, help complete the health summary on their behalf, and discuss your questions about their care during the consultation.
Is this suitable for urgent medical problems?

No. This consultation is a scheduled assessment, not emergency care — if you have an urgent or time-sensitive medical problem, please contact your local emergency services or treating physician immediately. Please also continue any care and medication advised by your treating physician; never stop a prescribed medicine without their guidance.

At Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village, our Ayurvedic outpatient (OPD) consultation offers a smooth, tailored treatment process based on traditional Ayurvedic principles. Visitors are greeted with a friendly reception, where an OPD form is filled out and their medical history is entered digitally for a natural healing consultation in Ayurveda. Next, there’s a comprehensive consultation with an Ayurvedic physician, including traditional Ayurvedic diagnosis, pulse examination, and personalized Ayurvedic treatment online or in person. A personalized wellness plan is developed according to your dosha and health state. Following that, you move on to therapies, which include Panchakarma detox and targeted treatments for issues such as arthritis, diabetes, stress relief, and skin ailments. Treatments are administered by skilled therapists utilizing, therapeutic oils and Kairali’s export-ready Ayurvedic products. After treatment, you are provided with herbal remedies along with detailed usage instructions, and a follow-up plan is arranged to ensure ongoing Ayurvedic care. For convenience, online consultations with an Ayurvedic physician in India are also offered.

Explore the archived Food Sadhana programme, including its 2017 highlights, daily practices, Ayurvedic meals and teacher biography.

In the journey to understand the Self, it is essential to begin with the obvious and progress to the finer aspects. The most essential element of our overall existence is food; it influences not just our physical body, but also our energetic self and mind! However, despite the essential role food plays in our physical and spiritual health, it frequently gets neglected or overshadowed by the demands of contemporary life. Food Sadhana encompasses a collection of spiritual practices and a lifestyle that acknowledges the sacred essence of our food – including what we consume, how it is prepared, how it is ingested, how it is processed, and how it exits the body – aiming to transform the individual into a living temple of the Self; a temple that is pristine and pure, where devotion and meditation continuously and effortlessly thrive.
When integrated with the principles of Ayurveda, Food Sadhana transforms into an intensely personal experience, yet a thoughtful, knowledgeable one.

Come and participate in the esteemed Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village in Kerala for a 9-day immersive Food Sadhana retreat. Pandit Dabral will lead you into the profound realm of the practical philosophy of Food Sadhana through daily satsang rooted in the Himalayan Tradition’s oral heritage. Pandit Tejomaya will lead you in the physical exercises that promote a clean and healthy body for a Food Sadhaka. The expert team of Ayurvedic doctors and personnel from Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village will provide customized therapies and amazing meals to make all of the practices a reality in your life!
This is a unique chance to elevate your sadhana to a level you never thought could be achieved.

About: Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village

The Ayurvedic Healing Village is located amid 65 acres of vibrant greenery in Palakkad, Kerala. It features 30 unique villas, all adhering to “Vastu Shastra” design – the Indian interpretation of feng shui. The retreat is enveloped by herbs and trees that possess great healing and rejuvenating properties, creating the perfect tranquil haven for relaxation! There is a large swimming pool, tennis facility, library, and gym amenities.

The retreat provides top-quality Ayurvedic therapies and therapeutic massages, featuring highly skilled massage therapists and physicians. They provide numerous therapies, such as Abhyangam, Pizhichil, Shirodhara, Panchakarma, and more.

Ayurveda & Yoga Retreat – Kerala, India

Set off on a unique journey to one of India’s most stunning southern states, Kerala. Blessed with beautiful landscapes, idyllic beaches, and breathtaking emerald backwaters, it’s no surprise that it ranks among “the paradises of the world” and “50 places of a lifetime,” according to National Geographic Traveller Magazine.
Terraced tea plantation on green hills with mist filling the valley and mountain peaks beyond

Our retreat offers a more relaxed atmosphere in the Palakkad district, situated at the base of the majestic and enchanting Western Ghats at Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village. Awarded ‘Best Luxury Destination Spa, 2012’ by World Luxury Spa Awards, your second home boasts all contemporary luxuries, including a swimming pool, gym, and tennis court. All of this is encircled by vast acres of organic Ayurvedic fields and extensive jungle.

During the retreat, you’ll meet with an Ayurvedic doctor who will recommend specific herbs and treatments tailored to your individual needs. You will reside in a deluxe villa with air conditioning, allocated based on your Zodiac sign. Every villa features a tranquil stream encircling it and adheres to “Vastu Shastra” (akin to Feng Shui) to foster harmony with nature and the universal energy flow.

Description of Treatment:

Abhyangam (General therapy): The individual receiving the treatment is positioned on the Droni (a wooden bed specifically designed for the therapy). Two masseuses are positioned on both sides of the individual, spreading herbal oil on the scalp and massaging softly. The treatment proceeds on the neck, ears, shoulders, chest, and back. The individual then lies on their back and the treatment proceeds from shoulders to toes. Throughout the therapy session, the individual reclines on their right side, left side, stomach, then back again, and ultimately in a seated posture. In Ayurvedic tradition, general therapy (Abhyangam) is used to support restful sleep, vitality and healthy skin. These treatments are also a form of preventive healthcare; in brief, they revitalize the body and sustain the physique.

Dhara

Dhara: The patient rests on a wooden bed in a relaxed posture. A uniquely crafted device is loaded with the therapeutic oil and positioned at a designated elevation. The masseur subsequently moves the device back and forth, allowing the oil to flow steadily and softly over the forehead. The head is subsequently dried with a towel, and oil is reapplied to it. This therapy can be applied to a specific area or the entire body, based on the condition. It encourages renewal and revitalization of the human body and mind, reducing the impact of aging. This is a unique treatment for stress and tension.

India’s first Mindfulness Retreat in Palakkad Kerala June 26-30
Guided by famous coach Santhosh Babu, Iyengar yoga specialist Raageshwari, and American Holotropic Breathwork professionals Sharanya and Dough.

A dozen specialists, including renowned coach Santhosh Babu, singer and actress Raageshwari, and American holotropic breathwork specialists Sharanya and Dough, will be part of India’s inaugural retreat on Mindfulness in Palakkad, Kerala. The five-day retreat offers tools and methodologies for the inner transformation of individuals keen to explore inner development.

“Mindfulness, as a concept, is gaining popularity with thousands of people showing interest in meditation, yoga, and mindfulness. Time magazine’s January 2014 cover story focused on ‘Mindfulness Revolution’ while the Wisdom 2.0 conference, held in San Francisco in February 2014, deliberated mindfulness”, says Retreat Director Santhosh Babu.

“This Mindfulness Retreat is for people who want to be self-aware and work on themselves. We look forward to working with 40-50 individuals — corporate executives, businessmen, and families — with an open mind, quest for greater understanding, and the will to explore more,” adds Santhosh Babu.

Well-known singer-actress Raageshwari is now a Facial and Iyengar yoga practitioner. She began a long journey of positivity and healing when she was diagnosed with Bell’s Palsy, a nervous disorder that leads to the paralysis of the facial muscles. As medicines could not help, she restored the strength of her facial muscles through facial yoga and Iyengar yoga, without reconstructive surgery.

“For me, the growth during the time I was ill, was huge. Today I know exactly what I want, and that became possible, because I had the time to rediscover myself, when I fell ill. Introduction to yoga, meditation, and holistic healing started to take over my life. If you really, really believe in something, it will come true,” says Raageshwari.

Additional session specialists consist of US-based Holotropic Breathwork instructor Sharanya Naik. Holotropic Breathwork is a technique created by Dr. Stanislav Grof to support psychedelic psychotherapy and serve as a substitute for LSD, which was previously utilized in therapy. This marks the inaugural time that Holotropic Breathwork will be instructed to the public in India.
Raji Prakash, co-chair of the Retreat, stated, “Participants will gain from self-awareness, mindfulness, general well-being, and personal growth.”

Shruti Nanda Poddar, a specialist in Vibrational and Sound healing, will assist attendees in connecting with their inner selves using the power of music. The Mindfulness Retreat will feature Kundalini Yoga and meditation sessions led by Anita Anand, as well as Pranic healing by Nidhi Jain and Shivani Hariharan.

The Retreat is engaging, and each hour at Kairali will guarantee that the body and mind are in harmony. A usual day would include yoga, expert workshops, various Ayurveda massages, music, and evaluations. Organic vegetarian cuisine, specially crafted by the Ayurveda centre, will enhance the transformative experience.

Santhosh Babu, the founder and managing director of Organisation Development Alternatives, assists organizations in transforming via leadership development and cultural change. Santhosh Babu, the writer of India’s inaugural book on coaching, is also a columnist and author. He instructs healers in hypnosis and is recognized for his hypnosis demonstrations at IIT Delhi, Mumbai, IIM Ahmedabad, and IIM Calcutta.

Abhyanga and oil therapies

Abhyanga is the synchronised application of warm herbal oil by two therapists, here along the legs, feet, shoulders and scalp. Pizhichil pours the oil from a brass vessel over the body; Udwarthanam works herbal powder into the skin instead of oil.

A key contributor to Kerala’s natural charm is its rivers, which flow gracefully through the state, enriching the land with fertility and beauty. The backwaters, framed by swaying palms and dotted with quaint villages, offer a unique way to experience Kerala’s natural allure. One of the best ways to explore this paradise is by embarking on a journey aboard a traditional houseboat, or Kettuvallom.

In earlier times, these houseboats were used for transporting grains and spices. Over time, they were transformed into floating havens for travelers, offering an unparalleled experience of the backwaters. Today, these houseboats are equipped with modern amenities, blending traditional charm with contemporary comfort. Many feature well-designed bedrooms with en-suite bathrooms, cozy living areas, and even kitchens. Some luxurious houseboats offer spacious decks or balconies, perfect for enjoying panoramic views of the serene waters and lush greenery.

A houseboat cruise through Kerala’s backwaters offers a unique perspective of rural life. The waterways weave through a complex network of lagoons, lakes, and canals, providing an intimate view of unspoiled natural beauty and vibrant local culture. Guests can enjoy the sights of verdant paddy fields, traditional fishing villages, and the daily rhythms of life along the banks.

Whether you’re a nature lover, a culture enthusiast, or simply seeking relaxation, the backwaters and rivers of Kerala promise an unforgettable experience. With their calm waters, breathtaking views, and the charm of houseboat living, these natural wonders invite you to unwind and reconnect with the beauty of the world around you.

Experience Kerala's Vibrant Festivals: Onam, Thrissur Pooram and More
Discover Kerala's rich culture through Onam, Thrissur Pooram, Pattambi Nercha, and more. Celebrate traditions with elephants, music, and artistic spectacles.
Pattambi Nercha
Festival Month: January to early March

The celebration of Pattambi Nercha honors Aloor Valiya Poolunjikoya Thangal, a pious Muslim from Malabar. Traditional musical ensembles such as Panchavadyam and Thayambaka are performed during this celebration. Art forms assume a breathtaking magnificence as the procession comes to an end on the riverbanks at midnight.
Konganpada festival Kerala
Konganpada of Chittur
Festival Month: February / March
Caparisoned elephants in gold headdresses under lit parasols at a night temple festival

Konganpada is a colorful celebration commemorating the Nairs of Chittur’s triumphs over the Konganadu (Coimbatore) militia, which was led by the Chola King Rajadhi Raja. It also commemorates their victory over the Kongus. It takes place in Kumbham on the first Monday following the gloomy lunar twilight. An hour-long drumming performance closes out the festival.
Nenmara Vallangi Vela

Palakkad village’s Nellikulangara Bhagavathy temple is the site of this celebration. The inhabitants of Nenmara and Vallangi villages jointly celebrate the Nellikulangara Bhagavathy on Pooram day of the Malayalam month of Meenam. A traditional flag-hoisting ceremony (Kodiyettam) kicks off the celebration. In addition to thirty adorned elephants, a variety of artistic disciplines, including Karivela, Kummatti, and Andivela, are displayed under an ornate canopy. Thrissur Pooram considers this group of two villages to be of the second highest importance.
Nenmara Vallangi Vela in kerala
Thrissur Pooram (At Thrissur)
Festival Month: April
Row of caparisoned elephants before a tiled-roof Kerala temple as dense crowds watch

The search for the best elephants begins in early April, and tenancies of elegant elephants are delivered to Thrissur for the Thrissur Pooram celebrations. The Cochin royal family founded the event in the 18th century to honor Vadakkumnathan Shiva. Elephants transport the deity during festival processions and temple circumambulations. The temple elephants are adorned with gold-plated caparisons (nettipattam), bells, and necklaces. People riding elephants hold tinseled silk parasols aloft, waving white tufts, and peacock feather fans to the beat of the music. Drums and nadhaswarams create devout musical scenes featuring elephants facing each other. The festival’s finale is a spectacular fireworks display.
Onam
Festival Month: August / September

Onam, the grand harvest festival of Kerala, is a vibrant celebration symbolizing unity, prosperity, and cultural heritage. This 10-day festival marks the homecoming of King Mahabali and showcases Kerala’s traditions through elaborate flower carpets (Pookalam), traditional dances like Kathakali and Thiruvathira, and the famous Onasadya feast served on banana leaves. Vallamkali (snake boat races) on serene backwaters and cultural performances add to the festive spirit. Onam reflects the essence of harmony and gratitude, bringing families and communities together to honor a bountiful harvest and cherish the richness of Kerala’s history and traditions. Wishing everyone a joyous and prosperous Onam!

Panchakarma – panch and karmas, when literally translated means ‘Five Procedures’. It is an ayurvedic treatment that involves elaborated methods of purification to release stress, which prepares the body tissues to accept the maximum benefits of food, nutrition and exercise.

The five procedures are Vamana (Emesis), Virechana (Purgation), Niroohavasti (Decoction enema), Nasya (Instillation of medicine through nostrils), and Anuvasanavasti (Oil enema). Panchkarma treatment is a three stage process—purva (pre-operative), pradhana (operative) and paschat (post-operative) measures. Ayurveda advises to practice Purvakarma because of the deep rooted imbalances in the body, which needs to be flushed out in the right way by Purvakarma and then by Panchkarma.

Those with an interest in complementary or holistic approaches to health should consider starting with the therapy that has the longest lineage. Ayurveda, the ancient health practice of India is thought by some historians to predate even ancient Egyptian medicine. Acknowledged as the inventor of modern day surgery, Ayurvedic Treatment and detoxification methods have remained popular for thousands of years, and their success now precipitates the worldwide spread of this natural and traditional wellbeing knowledge.

The first thing to learn about Ayurveda is that the body must always be viewed as a whole, rather than in its separate parts. This means accepting the body as part of an integrated system, involving mind, body and soul. Ayurveda offers curative, as well as preventative methods of health and understands that a united approach to lifestyle ensures true health and longevity.

While viewing all individuals as part of an interwoven community, Ayurveda also looks deeply into each individual. This is the reason that no two courses of Ayurveda Treatment can ever be the same. Guests undertake an initial consultation with one of our experienced and compassionate Ayurvedic doctors, who remain in a supervisory role in order to tailor their treatments perfectly to their body type and individual health needs.

Part of this initial consultation, or ‘Prakriti Analysis’ is the diagnosis of the individual’s body type, or Ayurvedic dosha. Ayurvedic dosha theory is built upon the ancient metaphysics of the five elements, which appear in different combinations in each of us, forming our unique individuality. The tri-dosha system consists of; Vata Dosha, representing ether and air; Pita Dosha representing fire and water; and Kapha Dosha, representing water and earth.

Do you arrange pick-up from the airport or railway station?Yes. The hospital can arrange a private car for arriving patients. Message our patient care team on WhatsApp, or call the main line, and share your arrival date, time and flight or train number. A team member will confirm the driver and vehicle details.

How will I recognise the driver?A Kairali representative waits for you in the arrivals area with a name-board. You receive the driver’s name and vehicle details before you land, so you know exactly who is picking you up.

Is pick-up available for late-evening arrivals?Yes. A pre-arranged transfer is recommended for late arrivals, when local roads are quiet. Share your flight details in advance and your driver will wait for you at any hour.

Can I come by train?Yes. Palakkad Junction (PGT) is the recommended station, around 18 km away — about a 35-minute drive. Taxis are available at the station, or send us your train number and arrival time and we will pick you up.

Is the trip safe for a solo traveller?Kerala is among the calmest regions of India, and English is widely spoken. With a pre-arranged transfer you are met by a named driver, so there is no need to look for a taxi on arrival. Many of our patients travel to us alone.

Can you accommodate a wheelchair or a caregiver?Yes. A wheelchair-accessible vehicle and an accompanying caregiver can be arranged. Please tell us your requirements at booking so the right vehicle is ready.

Do I need an Indian visa?Most international visitors need a valid passport and an Indian visa or an eligible e-Visa. Requirements vary by nationality and can change — please check the official Government of India visa portal before you travel.

Is this a hospital or a spa?Kairali – The Ayurvedic Healing Village is an NABH-accredited Ayurvedic hospital. Care is led by registered Ayurvedic physicians, and every treatment programme begins with a clinical consultation. It is not a spa.

Identical viewBox 0 0 2993.4 1950.82, identical width/height, all 28 paths and their exact d values unchanged, class attributes retained, and only the three original colours applied. Ayurveda is Sanskrit and is a combination of the words Ayus, meaning life, and Veda, which means science; think of it as ‘the science of life’. Ayurveda is based on the principles of finding harmony and balance between mind, body and soul. The main focus is preventing disease and maintaining vitality and health by following recommendations specific to your type; these recommendations offer insight into the ideal routine of proper diet, lifestyle, behavior and state of mind. Ridding our systems of both physical and spiritual toxins is an important part of the practice.

Nathalie Geetha is a life-lover… After a career as a family physician, she decides to train in yogatherapy, dance, and Ayurveda, with Deepak Chopra. Following her guidance we will learn and practice together the principles of this ancient medicine. A manual will be offered to you so that you can experience the Detox at home when needed. *This detox program is inspired by Nathalie Geetha’s on-line program “Ma Détox Colorée”

Food is perhaps the most important and most neglected ingredient of a healthy lifestyle. The Ayurvedic cuisine is a type of new wave food system where the diet includes all the necessary minerals and nutrients to promote growth and health while also keeping in consideration the palatability of the food offered.

This dietary system takes into account all the possible permutations through which the quality of food can be increased without destroying its taste. This cuisine is not only healthy but it also caters to all the age groups according to their choices.

There is no dearth of variety and there are numerous dishes with varied preparations which help in maintaining the novelty of the food. This cuisine is the best way to promote a healthy lifestyle for everyone.
Kerala is one of the most charming and captivating states in India and this exceptional natural beauty claims for it being named to be “God’s Own Country”.

Houseboats in Kerala is a unique attraction which has gained the attention of tourists from all over the world. One cannot think of complete tours and travel in India without exploring the scenic backwaters with a stay in a Kerala boathouse.
What is unique about backwaters in Kerala ?
Kerala Backwaters are a network of interconnected canals, rivers, lakes and inlets, a labyrinthine system formed by more than 900 km of waterways.

In the midst of this landscape there are a number of towns and cities, which serve as the starting and end points of backwater cruises.The backwaters have a unique ecosystem – freshwater from the rivers meets the seawater from the Arabian Sea. Many unique species of aquatic life including crabs, frogs and mudskippers, water birds such as terns, kingfishers, darters and cormorants, and animals such as otters and turtles live in and alongside the backwaters. Palm trees, pandanus shrubs, various leafy plants and bushes grow alongside the backwaters, providing a green hue to the surrounding landscape.
