Bookings must be made by a patient aged 18 or above; minors are welcome when accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. There is no stated maximum age. Under-5s stay complimentary, ages 5–12 are charged 50% for food and extra bedding, and over-12s are charged in full.

Wake up before sunrise and sleep by 10 PM Practice mindful eating with fresh, seasonal foods Stay hydrated with warm water throughout the day Incorporate gentle movement like yoga or walking Practice oil pulling and self-massage (abhyanga) with appropriate oils Adjust your diet according to your dominant dosha (body constitution) Our physicians provide personalised recommendations during your stay.

Doshas are the three bodily energies— Vata (air and space), Pitta (fire and water), and Kapha (earth and water)—that govern all physical and mental processes. Understanding your unique dosha composition helps determine the most effective treatments, diet, and lifestyle practices for your constitution. At Kairali, we conduct a thorough dosha assessment upon arrival to customize your wellness program.

Yes. Ayurvedic physicians in India complete a five-and-a-half-year BAMS (Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery) degree that includes clinical training in Ayurvedic and modern medical practice. Many pursue further specialisation (MD in Ayurveda) over an additional three years. Ayurvedic medicine is recognised by the WHO and regulated in India by the Ministry of AYUSH. Read more on our Knowledge Centre .

Whether a programme suits you depends on your individual assessment, and Ayurvedic care is offered alongside, not instead of, the treatment you already receive. Our physicians see patients with concerns including: Digestive disorders (IBS, acid reflux, constipation) Respiratory conditions (asthma, allergies, sinusitis) Joint and muscular pain (arthritis, back pain) Stress-related disorders (anxiety, insomnia, fatigue) Skin conditions (psoriasis, eczema, acne) Metabolic disorders (diabetes, obesity, thyroid imbalances) Women’s health issues (PCOS, menopause, hormonal imbalances) Neurological conditions (migraines, nerve support therapy)

Kairali offers Ayurvedic programmes tailored to your constitution and health goals, each beginning at a physician-set minimum stay: Panchakarma & Detoxification — from 14 nights Stress Relief & Mental Wellness — from 7 nights Chronic condition support (arthritis, diabetes, hypertension, respiratory, neurological) — from 7 to 14 nights depending on the condition Weight Management & Metabolism — from 14 nights Women's Hormonal Balance & Endocrine Therapy — from 21 nights; Postpartum Rejuvenation — from 14 nights Musculoskeletal Care (back, neck, joints, spine) — from 14 nights Skin & Chronic Skin Conditions — from 14 nights Immunity Enhancement — from 7 nights Each programme includes daily prescribed therapies, a personalised diet, and yoga and meditation sessions. Internal herbal medicines, lab tests and specialty therapies are charged as needed. See full programme details on our programmes page .

Recommended stay length depends on your programme and is set by the physician at consultation: 3 nights — the Preventive Health & Regenerative programme, an introduction to Ayurveda 7 nights — stress relief, sleep, immunity and several other programmes 14 nights — Panchakarma, musculoskeletal, skin, weight-management and most chronic-condition programmes 21 nights — hormonal/endocrine and addiction-recovery programmes Our physicians confirm the exact duration for your condition at consultation.

Most programmes include two Ayurvedic therapies a day (one a day for the Preventive Health & Regenerative programme), alongside sunrise yoga and evening meditation. Some patients notice mild detoxification symptoms such as headaches, fatigue or digestive changes in the first few days — a normal sign of the body eliminating toxins, monitored by our physicians. Your physician adjusts your plan for comfort throughout.

Kerala has a warm, tropical climate with four seasons: Summer (March–May) — 28–38°C; warm, sunny days, good for pitta-pacifying treatments Monsoon (June–September) — 23–32°C; regular rainfall, the traditional season for intensive Panchakarma Post-monsoon/Autumn (October–November) — 24–32°C; pleasant, good for rejuvenation therapies Winter (December–February) — 20–30°C; mild days and cooler evenings, good for vata-balancing therapies

Essential items: Comfortable, loose-fitting cotton clothing Light shawl or sweater for evenings (especially December-February) Modest swimwear for the pool Walking shoes for nature trails Personal toiletries (we provide basic amenities) Medications and supplements you regularly take Journal for reflections during your stay For treatments and yoga: Extra sets of loose, cotton clothing (treatments involve oils) Light cotton scarf for meditation

Kairali is not currently empanelled with Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY), CGHS or other government schemes, and we do not offer cashless tie-ups with private insurers. Many patients claim reimbursement afterwards by submitting our invoices and medical documents to their insurer. We can provide detailed invoices, treatment summaries, prescriptions and admission/discharge notes to support a reimbursement claim, and can guide you on the documents insurers typically ask for. Final approval always depends on your insurer's policy.

More than 30 days before admission: full refund. 15 to 30 days before admission: 50% of the amount paid is refunded, less applicable transaction fees and taxes. Fewer than 15 days before admission, or a change of dates during the stay: no refund. See our Cancellation & Refund Policy page.

Most visitors to India need a tourist visa or e-visa; for Ayurvedic treatment, a Medical Visa or Medical Attendant Visa may be more appropriate, especially for stays over 60 days. Visa rules change, so check the official Indian visa portal (indianvisaonline.gov.in) or your local Indian consulate for current requirements before applying. We can provide an invitation letter to support your visa application on request.

Thiruvalathoor Temple
An ancient Bhagavathy temple known for its woodwork and stone sculpture. Local tradition tells of a surrounding wall left unfinished before daybreak.
Temple approach

A riverside memorial to Thunchath Ezhuthachan, whose Malayalam retellings of the Ramayana and Mahabharata shaped the language’s literary tradition. Manuscripts and objects associated with the poet are part of its heritage.
Gurumadam approach
Thenari Sree Rama Temple
A place of worship associated with the Ramayana, with a sacred spring beside the temple. Its water is revered in local tradition.
Sree Rama Theertham approach
Palakkad Fort · Tipu’s Fort
Built by Hyder Ali in 1766, this protected fort is one of Palakkad’s best-known landmarks. Its moat, ramparts and grounds offer a view of the town’s history; the Anjaneya shrine stands inside.
Fort road approach; walk to entrance
Jainimedu Jain Temple
A historic granite temple dedicated to Chandraprabha, with images of Jain Tirthankaras. The surrounding neighbourhood is also associated with poet Kumaran Asan and Veenapoovu.
Visit the Vishwanatha Swamy temple and the surrounding agraharam streets. Kalpathy is especially known for its annual chariot festival, Ratholsavam.
Vishwanatha Swamy temple
Kerala Kalamandalam
At Cheruthuruthy, this renowned institution preserves Kerala’s traditional performing arts. Arrange a visitor programme in advance if you hope to see teaching or performances.
Campus road approach

Also known as the Moonnumoorthy temple, this riverside temple is associated with Shiva, Vishnu and Sankaranarayana. Its traditional koothambalam, or temple theatre, is an important architectural feature.
Explore a village on the Bharathapuzha known for its temple traditions and the historic Kattil Madom monument nearby. Allow additional travel for individual sites around the village.
Thrithala village centre
The Sree Krishna temple is one of Kerala’s important pilgrimage destinations, known for devotional offerings such as Thulabharam. Check temple entry rules and arrangements before travelling.
Road approach near Sree Krishna temple
An amusement and water park near Malampuzha, with activities for families. Check the park’s current opening schedule, available rides and entry requirements before visiting.
Park entrance approach
Malampuzha Rock Garden
Designed by Nek Chand, the garden turns discarded tiles, bangles, stones and other materials into sculpture. A distinctive art stop in the Malampuzha area.
Rock Garden approach
Malampuzha Dam & Gardens
The reservoir, dam and gardens sit below the surrounding hills. The area is also known for Kanayi Kunhiraman’s Yakshi sculpture and the aerial ropeway.
Dam approach
Meenkara Dam
A reservoir set in the countryside near the Kerala–Tamil Nadu border. The dam and surrounding landscape make a quieter stop for views of the water and hills.
Dam road approach
Pothundy Dam
An old earthen dam near Nenmara, with reservoir views and a backdrop of the Nelliyampathy hills. It can be a stop on the route towards Nelliyampathy.
Meenvallam Waterfalls
A forest waterfall on the Thuppanadu river in the Kalladikodan hills. Access involves walking beyond the road approach; check seasonal restrictions and local entry arrangements.
Nearest mapped road; final walk extra

Nelliyampathy

Attappadi
